rv.q: This production is most enjoyable as a whole—because of all the talent onstage, because of all the enthusiasm shown by every single member of the cast, and because of all the hard work that has obviously been put into the show by everyone involved with Music Theater Works.
This 21st century retelling of Stephen Schwartz’s hit musical from the 1970’s is dynamic and exciting.
But as distractions from ordinary life go in general, Pippin offers a provocative escape.
Its playfulness is a nice summer escape!

Music Theater Works’ production of Pippin directed by the company’s artistic director Kyle A. Dougan, choreographed by Mollyanne Nunn and Kaitlyn Pasquinelli, and with music direction by Justin Akira Kono, is one of the best shows you are going to see in Chicago this season.
With his strong voice and just the right touch, Ripperger plays Pippin to perfection and neatly carries the entire show.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically praise Music Theater Works' inventive "Pippin," celebrating its eclectic, pop culture-infused staging and fresh take on Schwartz's musical about a young man's existential journey, calling it wacky fun unlike any other production.
